facts.claim: Reactive Resume is a free, open-source resume builder.
Reactive Resume can be run on your own server with Docker, Kubernetes or Vercel.
Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app, and says your data stays yours and you choose what to keep private or share.
Memos is open-source software under the MIT license, and hosting may still cost money depending on the hardware or provider chosen.
Uptime Kuma is described on its GitHub repository as a self-hosted monitoring tool.
Before every upgrade, the Memos upgrade guide says to back up the database and attachments.
The default path for a Compose file is compose.yaml (preferred) or compose.yml in the working directory.
The Compose services reference example maps host port 8080 to container port 80 with "8080:80".
The Compose services reference describes restart unless-stopped as restarting the container regardless of exit code until the service is stopped or removed.
A top-level volumes declaration configures named volumes that can be reused across multiple services.
Docker Compose reads a .env file in the project directory to substitute variables such as ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} in the Compose file.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide runs two containers, the app and PostgreSQL, and PostgreSQL is reachable only from the app container.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide maps the app's container port 3000 to host port 3000 and says any free host port can be used.
In the Reactive Resume compose file, the app service depends on postgres with condition service_healthy.
Uploaded pictures live in the reactive_resume_data volume mounted at /app/data, and the app reads its settings with env_file .env.
Reactive Resume requires three settings: APP_URL, DATABASE_URL and AUTH_SECRET.
Docker's published-ports documentation says the -p or --publish flag makes a port available outside the host.
Memos stores its data in /var/opt/memos inside the container, and its Compose example maps ./data to that folder.
docker compose up with --wait exits once the services are running or healthy.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide's setup command is docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 180.
The Reactive Resume image has a built-in health check, so Compose reports the app as healthy once it is ready.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide generates AUTH_SECRET with openssl rand -hex 32 on Linux and macOS, and gives a PowerShell 7 command for Windows.
The first start of the Reactive Resume app creates its database tables, and you are signed in right after creating an account.
Without SMTP settings, Reactive Resume sends no verification email, so the address stays unverified, while the app can still be used.
docker compose ps lists the containers of a Compose project with their current status and exposed ports.
docker compose logs displays log output from the services.
Changing AUTH_SECRET signs everyone out and makes data encrypted with it unreadable, including two-factor authentication secrets.
ENCRYPTION_SECRET must be at least 32 characters and different from AUTH_SECRET, and it is required for saving personal AI and web-access keys.
Changes take effect after a restart, and with Docker Compose you run docker compose up -d to recreate the container with the new environment.
FLAG_DISABLE_SIGNUPS set to true stops new accounts from being created, and existing accounts keep working.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide suggests adding FLAG_DISABLE_SIGNUPS to .env after your own account exists, then running docker compose up -d.
The Reactive Resume repository's own compose file uses default passwords for PostgreSQL and SeaweedFS and keeps their ports off the host.
Docker Compose can mount a secret as a file under /run/secrets/<secret_name> inside the container.
Memos supports _FILE variable suffixes, so credentials can be passed from Docker secrets instead of plain environment variables.
A .gitignore file in the root directory of a repository tells Git which files and directories to ignore when making a commit.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide dumps the PostgreSQL database with pg_dump and restores it into an empty database with pg_restore.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide says the uploads can be backed up by copying the reactive_resume_data volume, or the folder you mounted yourself.
Without the same AUTH_SECRET and ENCRYPTION_SECRET, a restored Reactive Resume instance signs everyone out, breaks two-factor authentication and loses saved AI and Firecrawl keys.
pg_dump with the custom format writes a custom-format archive suitable for input into pg_restore.
pg_restore restores a PostgreSQL database from an archive created by pg_dump in one of the non-plain-text formats.
Reactive Resume's image tags include latest for the newest release and v6, which pins the major version and gets fixes without jumping to the next major version.
docker compose pull pulls the images of services defined in a compose.yaml file without starting containers based on them.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide says PostgreSQL is updated separately, and pulling a new app image does not change the database server's major version.
Volumes are easier to back up or migrate than bind mounts, and a Docker data volume persists after you delete the container that used it.

Docker's volume guide shows a backup pattern: a temporary container with --volumes-from reads the volume and writes a tar archive into a host folder mounted at /backup, and a restore pattern unpacks it.
Memos applies database migrations automatically on startup, downgrading after a migration has run is not supported, and the backup is the rollback path.
The Uptime Kuma update guide re-pulls the latest image and creates another container with the same volume.
Uptime Kuma recommends the tag 2 for the latest version 2 release, and says the latest tag is deprecated and points to version 1.
The Memos Docker Compose example uses the image neosmemo/memos:stable, publishes port 5230 and maps ./data to /var/opt/memos.
The Memos Docker guide says the stable tag is the safest default for production, while latest is development-oriented.
A fresh Memos instance started without MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL initializes private access.
The Memos MEMOS_DRIVER variable defaults to sqlite, the default database backend.
The Memos Docker Compose guide lists docker compose down, docker compose up -d and docker compose logs -f among its common operational commands.

Uptime Kuma's install page gives the command docker run -d --restart=unless-stopped -p 3001:3001 -v uptime-kuma:/app/data louislam/uptime-kuma:2, and says Uptime Kuma is then running on http://localhost:3001.
Uptime Kuma's install page says file locking support is required to avoid SQLite database corruption, and asks for the /app/data folder to map to a local directory or volume.
Reactive Resume is an open-source resume builder under the MIT license.
Uptime Kuma is described on its GitHub repository as a self-hosted monitoring tool.
docker compose ps lists containers for a Compose project with their current status and exposed ports.
docker compose logs --tail sets how many lines are shown from the end of each container's log, and -f follows the log output.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide lists the log messages Invalid environment variables, Database migrations failed, ECONNREFUSED and Local storage path is not writable, and gives the cause of each.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide says the app runs as the node user with UID 1000, and that user must be able to write to the mounted data folder.
APP_URL must match the address in the browser's address bar exactly, including https://, or sign-in redirects go to the wrong place.
The Reactive Resume Docker guide says to map the app's container port 3000 to any free host port.
The health endpoint /api/health answers 200 when everything is healthy and 503 when any check fails, and restarting the app does not fix a database or storage outage.
Docker's published-ports documentation says the -p or --publish flag makes a port available outside the host.
Uptime Kuma's install page shows how to change the published port with -p <YOUR_PORT>:3001.
A Docker data volume persists after you delete the container that used it.
